name: Skew Heap
description: A self-adjusting heap-ordered binary tree that is a simpler variant of the leftist heap. The key difference is that skew heaps unconditionally swap left and right children after every merge step, rather than checking ranks. This eliminates the need to store rank information while achieving the same O(log n) amortized bounds. Like leftist heaps, all operations are built on merge: insert merges a single-node tree, and extractMin removes the root and merges the two subtrees.

pseudocode.text: if h1 = null then return h2
if h2 = null then return h1
if h1.key > h2.key then swap h1, h2
swap h1.left and h1.right    // always swap
if heap = null then return null

testCases.name: Insert with unconditional child swaps
testCases.description: Each insert merges along the right spine and unconditionally swaps children at every visited node, causing the tree shape to change with each operation

testCases.name: Extract min with subtree merge
testCases.description: Extracting the minimum removes the root and merges left and right subtrees with unconditional swaps at every merge step

testCases.name: Amortized efficiency demonstration
testCases.description: Decreasing insertions followed by extractions demonstrate how unconditional swaps keep the tree approximately balanced over a sequence of operations, achieving O(log n) amortized cost
